control_results.score_rationale: The policy documents that information security policies are defined, approved, and aligned with legal requirements. There is evidence of defined processes for communication and assignment of responsibility, but there is insufficient detail on formal publication and specific mechanisms for communicating policies to relevant external parties.
evidence: Provider established an Information Security Program (the “Program”) to assure compliance with applicable laws. As required by law, the Program provides for the security and confidentiality of personal identifying information or sensitive personal information...

It is the policy of Provider to comply, and to require its employees to comply, with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, as well as Provider’s policies and procedures, governing information security...
The Program is universally applicable to all services offered by Provider...
The Coordinator will be responsible for maintaining a high level of awareness and sensitivity to safeguarding Information within all departments.
The Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring that company staff is trained in the relevant legal requirements for handling and storing Information.
gaps: No explicit mention of formal management approval process for the policies.
Lack of details on how policies are published and communicated to all employees.
No evidence of communication of policies to relevant external parties.
No reference to regular review and update frequency for the policies.
recommendations: Document a formal process for management approval of all information security policies.
Clearly state and implement procedures for publishing policies (e.g., company intranet, distribution upon onboarding).
Define and document processes for communicating applicable security policies to external parties (vendors, partners) as relevant.
Include requirements and procedures for periodic review and updates of all information security policies.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy assigns broad information security responsibilities, particularly to a Coordinator, and addresses access management and workforce security at a high level, but lacks specificity regarding segregation of duties and ongoing contact with authorities or special interest groups.
evidence: "The Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring that company staff is trained in the relevant legal requirements for handling and storing Information... The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards..." (Excerpt 1)

"Workforce security. Policies and procedures to ensure that all company employees have appropriate access to electronic Information and to prevent any unauthorized company employees from obtaining access... Procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of company employees who work with electronic Information... Procedures to determine that the access of a company employee to electronic Information is appropriate." (Excerpt 2)

"Policies and procedures that, based upon the entity’s access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process." (Excerpt 3)
gaps: No explicit mention or process for segregation of duties.
No details or requirements about maintaining contact with authorities or special interest groups.
Allocation of security responsibilities is centralized to the Coordinator without clearly defined roles for other positions.
No accountability framework or metrics for monitoring the effectiveness of these responsibilities.
recommendations: Explicitly define and document information security responsibilities across all relevant roles and departments, not just the Coordinator.
Implement and formalize procedures for segregation of duties, specifying which functions must not be performed by the same individual.
Establish processes for maintaining contact with relevant authorities and special interest groups, including responsible personnel and frequency of contact.
Include mechanisms for measuring and monitoring the effectiveness and compliance with defined responsibilities, such as metrics or periodic audits.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy establishes documented requirements for securing mobile devices and teleworking, including authentication, access controls, encryption, and risk assessment. However, it lacks evidence of ongoing measurement, monitoring, or structured integration with risk management beyond periodic assessments.
evidence: Individuals who wish to opt-in to BYOD must be authorized by management and must explicitly accept the requirements laid out in this policy.
PODs must use appropriate forms of device authentication approved by Provider’s IT department, such as digital certificates created for each specific device.
Remote access should be strictly controlled, using one-time password authentication.
All Provider departments must employ technical safeguards to ensure that electronically stored Information is secure from unauthorized access or use.

All hosts used by the employee that are connected to the Provider Internet/Intranet/Extranet, whether owned by the employee or Provider, shall be continually executing approved virus-scanning software with a current virus database...
gaps: No mention of specific monitoring or review mechanisms for mobile device and teleworking controls.
No details on how compliance with mobile or remote work policies is verified or enforced.
No explicit requirements for regular re-evaluation of remote work or mobile devices security in light of new risks.
Lack of user awareness/training initiatives specifically tailored for mobile/remote working.
No reference to metrics or KPIs to assess the effectiveness of mobile and teleworking controls.
recommendations: Implement and document regular reviews or audits of mobile device and teleworking arrangements to ensure ongoing compliance.
Establish formal metrics or KPIs to monitor the effectiveness of mobile/teleworking security measures.
Mandate recurring training for users on mobile device and teleworking risks and security practices.
Define enforcement mechanisms, such as periodic compliance checks for BYOD devices.
Integrate mobile and teleworking risks more explicitly into the organization's overall risk management processes.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy mentions compliance with applicable laws and general workforce security, but it does not explicitly require background verification checks for candidates, nor does it provide processes for such checks prior to employment.
evidence: It is the policy of Provider to comply, and to require its employees to comply, with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, as well as Provider’s policies and procedures, governing information security, confidentiality, and privacy.

Workforce security. Policies and procedures to ensure that all company employees have appropriate access to electronic Information and to prevent any unauthorized company employees from obtaining access to electronic Information.
Procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of company employees who work with electronic Information or in locations where it might be accessed;
gaps: No explicit mention of background verification checks for all candidates for employment.
No description of the process, responsibilities, or requirements for conducting background checks.
No reference to carrying out checks 'in accordance with relevant laws, regulations and ethics.'
recommendations: Add a policy statement requiring background verification checks for all employment candidates.
Outline the types of background checks to be performed and ensure alignment with relevant local, state, and federal laws.

Document procedures for recording, reviewing, and updating results of such checks.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy establishes formal, documented expectations for employee and contractor compliance with information security policies, provides supporting processes for training, access management, sanctions, and monitoring, but lacks explicit, organization-wide definitions for performance metrics, ongoing monitoring, or detailed role-based accountabilities.
evidence: Appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with security policies and procedures.

Policies and procedures to ensure that all company employees have appropriate access to electronic Information and to prevent any unauthorized company employees from obtaining access to electronic Information.
The Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring that company staff is trained in the relevant legal requirements for handling and storing Information.
Security awareness and training. A security awareness and training program for all company employees (including management).

All risk assessments must identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Information ... The assessment, at a minimum, must include employee training and management...
gaps: No defined metrics or mechanisms for monitoring employee compliance with information security during employment.
Accountability for ongoing adherence (beyond initial training and oversight by the Coordinator) is not detailed.
Contractor obligations are implied but not clearly or consistently addressed.
Continuous improvement or integration with risk management activities during the period of employment is not explicitly included.
recommendations: Establish and document ongoing monitoring processes, with defined metrics, to assess employee and contractor compliance with information security policies and procedures.
Explicitly outline role-based accountability for management, employees, and contractors during employment.
Include clear requirements and processes for contractors applying organizational security procedures, equivalent to those for employees.
Integrate periodic effectiveness reviews of the control into the organization’s risk management or continuous improvement processes.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy addresses termination of access to electronic information when employment ends and assigns responsibility for oversight, but does not clearly define, communicate, or enforce post-employment information security responsibilities and duties.
evidence: Procedures for terminating access to electronic Information under appropriate circumstances, such as, for example, when the employment of a company employee ends.

Provider will routinely monitor its operations related to the handling of the Information.
gaps: No explicit definition or documentation of post-employment information security responsibilities (e.g., ongoing confidentiality obligations).
No outlined process to communicate or reinforce such responsibilities at or after termination or change of employment.

recommendations: Define in writing the continuing information security responsibilities that persist beyond employment, such as confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations.
Establish a formal process to communicate these ongoing responsibilities to individuals upon termination or change of employment (e.g., exit interviews, signed acknowledgements).
Implement enforcement mechanisms for post-employment obligations, and document actions to be taken in case of violations.
Periodically review and update related procedures and provide refresher notifications to former employees where appropriate.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy discusses general safeguards, risk assessment, and access controls, but lacks explicit statements about identifying assets and maintaining a formal asset inventory as required by the control.
evidence: Provider will take steps to identify and assess internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Information...
The Coordinator will establish procedures for identifying and assessing risks in each relevant area of Provider’s operations...

gaps: No explicit requirement to identify assets associated with information and information processing facilities.
No formal process described for drawing up and maintaining an inventory of these assets.

recommendations: Add a policy statement that requires identification of all assets (hardware, software, data, etc.) related to information and information processing facilities.
Define a formal process for creating, maintaining, and periodically reviewing an asset inventory.
Ensure accountability for asset inventory management and specify roles responsible for maintaining it.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy frequently refers to access, confidentiality, and criticality, but it does not establish a formal process for the classification of information by value, sensitivity, legal requirements, or risk of disclosure/modification. Elements of classification are implied but not defined or managed programmatically.
evidence: assessment of the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components
confidentiality of business records containing personal identifying information or sensitive personal information as those terms may be defined by applicable law
information access management. Policies and procedures for authorizing access ... consistent with applicable law and best practices
security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level
gaps: No mention of a formal information classification scheme or process.
No clear assignment of classification levels (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) based on value, criticality, sensitivity, or legal requirements.
No requirements for labeling, handling, or marking information based on its classification.
No guidelines or policy for periodic review or reclassification of information.
recommendations: Establish and document a formal information classification policy with defined levels based on legal, business, and sensitivity criteria.
Assign responsibilities for classifying information and ensure periodic review and updates as business and regulatory requirements evolve.
Develop procedures for labeling, handling, storing, and transmitting classified information.
Train employees on the classification scheme and their responsibilities for protecting information at the appropriate level.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy outlines several high-level procedures for device and media controls, including the removal, re-use, and disposal of media, but lacks specificity and clear linkage to the organization's information classification scheme.

Policies and procedures to address the final disposition of electronic Information, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored.
Procedures for removal of electronic Information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.
A record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefor.

Lacks details on secure storage, labeling, transport, and accountability processes tied to classification levels.
No mention of regular review or monitoring of media handling procedures.
recommendations: Explicitly reference the organization’s classification scheme within the media handling procedures, ensuring different classes of information have appropriate protection.
Define and document specific security requirements for handling, storage, transport, and disposal of removable media by classification level.
Establish clear roles and responsibilities for staff managing media based on its classification.
Develop mechanisms for regular review, monitoring, and enforcement of compliance with media handling procedures.
Provide targeted training on media handling requirements based on classification levels as part of the security awareness program.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy establishes a documented access control policy, describes authorization, reviewing, and revocation procedures, and is linked to business and security requirements. However, explicit review frequency, metrics, or continuous improvement are not addressed.
evidence: Policies and procedures to ensure that all company employees have appropriate access to electronic Information and to prevent any unauthorized company employees from obtaining access to electronic Information.

Policies and procedures that, based upon the entity’s access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.

Policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic Information that are consistent with applicable law and best practices related to information security.

A unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy defines processes for secure log-on, password strength, failed login handling, and account identification/authorization, but lacks detailed metrics, ongoing monitoring, or explicit continuous improvement mechanisms.

Passwords must be unknown, unrecorded, and unrecoverable by system administrators or system support staff. ... All passwords must be at least 6 characters long and contain at least one letter and one number. Users will be required to change their password at least every 90 days.

There must be a limit to the number of repeated unsuccessful attempts to log into an application or server that deals with Information. For example, a system that 'locks' access from a particular account after 3 failed attempts would meet this criterion.
A unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
Person or entity authentication. Procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic Information is the one claimed.

recommendations: Define more comprehensive password quality requirements (such as complexity, reuse prohibition, detection of common passwords, and minimum change intervals).

Policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.
Policies and procedures, based upon the entity’s access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.
The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment.

control_results.control_name: Compliance with Legal and Contractual Requirements
control_results.score_rationale: The policy explicitly requires compliance with relevant laws and regulations, assigns responsibility, mandates risk assessment and monitoring, and ensures staff are trained on legal requirements. However, it lacks detailed procedures for systematically identifying, documenting, and updating legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements, and does not describe mechanisms for keeping this documentation current.
evidence: Provider established an Information Security Program (the “Program”) to assure compliance with applicable laws. As required by law, the Program provides for the security and confidentiality of personal identifying information or sensitive personal information collected...

It is the policy of Provider to comply, and to require its employees to comply, with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, as well as Provider’s policies and procedures, governing information security, confidentiality, and privacy.
The Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring that company staff is trained in the relevant legal requirements for handling and storing Information.
Provider will designate an Information Security Program Coordinator (“Coordinator”) who will be primarily responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Program.

Provider will take steps to identify and assess internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Information that could result in the unauthorized access, disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction or other compromise of such Information.
gaps: No formal process for identifying, documenting, and evaluating relevant legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
Absence of procedures for keeping legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements documentation up to date.
No explicit mention of a register or record of these requirements, or how contractual obligations are tracked.
recommendations: Establish and document a formal process for identifying and cataloging all relevant legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements impacting information security.
Implement procedures to regularly review and update the documentation of these requirements, including maintaining a compliance register.
Define accountability for monitoring changes in legal and regulatory requirements and updating the compliance records accordingly.
Include a mechanism for tracking contractual obligations related to information security and ensuring ongoing compliance.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy defines periodic independent reviews of the information security program, assigns responsibility to a Coordinator, and requires regular monitoring and reporting, but does not detail the independence of reviewers or the specific metrics/monitoring mechanisms, nor does it explicitly tie the process to risk management or continuous improvement.
evidence: This Program will be reviewed and adjusted periodically. The Coordinator will review the Program annually to ensure ongoing compliance, as well as consistency with other existing and future laws and regulations.
The Coordinator will provide periodic reports on the status of the Program and note any changes to the overall risk assessment and changes to established safeguards.

Some areas of the company may require more frequent review than others, such as IT, records management, or any other area that comes in contact with a high volume of Information or is especially vulnerable to technological or procedural risks and threats.
The Coordinator will establish procedures for identifying and assessing risks in each relevant area of Provider’s operations outlined above.

The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment, and will regularly monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards.
gaps: No explicit mention of the reviews being performed independently (by a party not responsible for implementation).
Lacks details on monitoring/measuring the effectiveness of the review program (metrics, KPIs, etc.).
Does not describe how results of reviews are integrated into risk management or used for continuous improvement.
No mention of formal accountability or ownership for review findings beyond the Coordinator.
recommendations: Specify that security reviews should be conducted by an independent party, either internal (not responsible for implementation) or external.
Define clear metrics and measurement criteria to evaluate the effectiveness of the information security program and its controls.
Establish accountability processes for addressing findings from reviews, assigning action owners and timelines.
Explicitly integrate review outcomes into the organization's structured risk management and continuous improvement processes.
